newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says a healthy Mexico is in U.S.'s interest.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says a healthy Mexico is in U.S.'s interest.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Friday praised Mexican economic reform efforts and said its participation in the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) has helped it achieve financial stability.

"Mexico today is growing at a healthy rate, a result of its economic reforms, including NAFTA," Rubin said in remarks prepared for delivery at a briefing to hail the first three years of the NAFTA pact between the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Rubin said Mexican unemployment and inflation were down, monetary and fiscal policy remained on track, and foreign capital has returned now that the country has weathered a financial crisis that began in 1995.
"There are many challenges ahead, but much has been accomplished," Rubin said.
He added a healthy, growing Mexico was "very much in the national economic and security interests of the United States."
A prosperous and stable Mexico also is better able to work with the United States on a variety of other issues including immigration and drugs, Rubin noted.
